newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Saflife plans shr capital rise for JCI buy.
newsitem.headline: Saflife plans shr capital rise for JCI buy.

text.p: Saflife Ltd said on Friday it planned to increase its share capital from 30.2 million rand to 130.2 million rand to facilitate the purchase of a stake in mining house JCI Ltd.
It said the additional funds may also be used to hold a rights offer to finance all or part of the purchase.

The African Mining Group, a consortium including Capital Alliance Holdings Ltd (Captall) and other black interests, last month sealed a deal to buy a 34.9 percent stake in JCI from Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd for 2.88 billion rand.
Saflife controls 25.9 percent of Captall and was earlier earmarked as the likely vehicle through which the deal would be financed.

The deal, which gives black business a significant stake in the South African mining industry for the first time, sets the scene for a bid by the consortium to buy Anglo's remaining 12.7 percent stake in the mining house, giving it unfettered control of JCI.
